correctness.rationale: For the cyclic perfect two-dimensional evolution algebra e1^2=e2, e2^2=e1, e1e2=0 over any field, expanding weight-lambda Rota-Baxter identity gives exactly six polynomial equations in a,b,c,d (column convention). These imply (a+d+lambda)b=(a+d+lambda)c=0 and b,c either both zero or both nonzero. Diagonal nonzero solutions give t=a/d with (t-1)(t^2-t+1)=0; t=1 yields -lambda I and the other roots require (t+1)d=-lambda. Off-diagonal solutions satisfy trace a+d+lambda=0 and b=(a-d)u^2,c=-(a-d)u with u^3=1, and the same t relation. For nonzero weight the count is exactly 2 or 10 according to primitive cubic roots, including char2/char3. For zero weight only char3 permits nonzero solutions, on two distinct k-linear lines with intersection {0}; over finite fields char3 count 2q-1. This covers all field characteristics, not just finite enumerations. Independent direct enumeration of four matrix entries over F2,F3,F5,F7 for weights 0,1 gave counts (1,2),(5,2),(1,2),(1,10), matching classification. Symbolic proof supplies unrestricted quantifiers.
